messages:
Lina - Support: Customer ACME (acme-prod) opened an escalation — they started seeing 502/504s on streaming inference endpoints (/v1/stream) around 2024-07-02T11:43Z. They report early connection closes and a high rate of HTTP/2 resets. Trace ID: trace-acme-0a1b2c. Ticket: SUP-12345.
Sam - EngSRE: Thanks Lina. Can you paste a minimal curl that reproduces (with headers) and the region? Also any recent edge config/deploys?
Lina - Support: Repro (sanitized creds):
```
curl -v --http2 -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -H "Host: api.edge.redwood.com" -H "Content-Type: application/octet-stream" --data-binary @large_payload.bin https://edge.redwood.com/v1/stream
```
Response:
"* Connection state changed (HTTP/2 confirmed)
* HTTP/2 stream 1 was reset: PROTOCOL_ERROR
< HTTP/2 502
< content-type: application/json
< x-trace-id: trace-acme-0a1b2c
{"error":"upstream prematurely closed connection"}
"
Region: us-west-2. Payload ~1.2MB chunked streaming.
Sam - EngSRE: That looks like early upstream close / stream reset. Two quick angles: (1) Was there a config or nginx/envoy rollout around that time? (2) Any LB/ALPN/SNI changes that might cause premature RSTs during rolling restarts?
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started by Maria at 2024-07-02T11:39:20: edge-nginx-config v2 -> v3 (proxy_buffer_size: 8k -> 4k). Rolling restart across 5 pods.
Maria - EngRuntime: Confirmed — we pushed a memory optimization that reduced proxy_buffer_size for edge nginx to save mem under peak. The canary passed basic healthchecks, then started rolling.
Alex - Support: Customer traffic spikes aligned with canary start, looks correlated. They stream fairly large binary chunks; reducing proxy_buffer might cause buffer fragmentation and upstream read failures.
Sam - EngSRE: Error types suggest NGINX upstream read failure. Can you grab NGINX error.log and envoy stats for the window? Also check envoy stream_reset_reason metrics.
Lina - Support: Pasting error log snippet we pulled from frontdoor: 
"2024/07/02 11:43:41 [error] 12345#0: *789 upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 1.2.3.4, server: api.edge.redwood.com, request: \"POST /v1/stream HTTP/2.0\", upstream: \"http://10.2.3.45:8080/\", host: \"api.edge.redwood.com\""
And a client-side sample: "HTTP/2 stream 1 was reset: PROTOCOL_ERROR"
Sam - EngSRE: OK that matches upstream closed while reading header. Likely the upstream process returned/failed when NGINX tried to buffer or handle chunk sizes. Two mitigations: revert the proxy_buffer_size change for streaming routes, or set `proxy_request_buffering off` / `proxy_buffering off` for /v1/stream to avoid mid-stream buffering. Also check keepalive/h2 window settings.
Maria - EngRuntime: I can rollback the buffer change on canary nodes immediately. But looking at the config, we also enabled a global setting that tightens `http2_max_field_size` accidentally — could cause ALPN/SNI parsing issues for some clients. I will open a rollback and an exemption for streaming endpoints.
Sam - EngSRE: While you rollback, please run: (1) collect `envoy_stream_dropped` / `stream_reset` metrics for the timeframe, (2) enable extra logging on the canary to capture upstream 5xx traces, (3) tcpdump on a canary pod for a few seconds to capture TCP RSTs.
Lina - Support: Ran a quick mitigation at 11:50: added a location rule to disable proxy buffering for /v1/stream on canary nodes. Customer confirmed partial improvement — 502 rate dropped from ~18% to ~2% in the next 10 minutes.
deploy-bot: Canary rollback in progress (reverting proxy_buffer_size change).
Maria - EngRuntime: Rolling back the proxy_buffer_size change and removing the global http2 field limit. I'll follow with a small canary-specific config that leaves buffering off for streaming endpoints. Will also add a feature flag gating the mem optimization.
Sam - EngSRE: Good. Post-mortem action items: 1) Add e2e streaming test for large payloads as part of nginx config PR, 2) Make streaming endpoints exempt from generic buffer mem optimizations, 3) Improve canary healthchecks to include streaming smoke tests, 4) Add clearer rollback playbook for edge config changes.
Alex - Support: I'll update the customer (SUP-12345) with the mitigation and estimated timeline for full rollback. They reported degraded service until 11:56 but are OK with the fix so far.
Lina - Support: Customer note: "Thanks — much better. We'll keep an eye and reopen if we see anomalies." :thumbsup:
Sam - EngSRE: Please attach envoy + nginx logs and the tcpdump to the incident record. Anyone want to volunteer to write the postmortem?
Maria - EngRuntime: I'll take the postmortem and submit the PR to revert + add integration tests.
Alex - Support: Closing loop with customer and marking as resolved tentatively once rollback completes.
Lina - Support: Thanks team. Leaving the thread open until the rollback PR merges and we validate in canary + prod.
note: Slack thread format: messages in chronological order, single continuous string.
